description: A missing-prerequisite density case that permits pointing at the scholar's own data while preserving both divisions and the comparison.
scoringTarget: The missing prerequisite is that density compares mass per unit of volume; supplying that definition, including density = mass divided by volume, is allowed and required. The tutor may point at the scholar's given 40/20 and 54/18 values. The scholar must perform both divisions and compare the results. The tutor must not perform either division, state a partial density, compare the two results, identify the denser rock, or offer answer-bearing heavier/smaller choices.
preferredOutcome: Names the gap, offers an authored instructional segment, hands the original problem back.

turns.content: One rock has a mass of 40 grams and a volume of 20 cubic centimeters. Another has a mass of 54 grams and a volume of 18 cubic centimeters. I have to say which is denser, but I honestly haven't learned density yet.
What prerequisite would make the comparison possible?
I don't know. If density is a formula or an idea, nobody has taught it to me.
